chapter: Ben Pollack band and New York
title: Fired for dirty shoes; Goodman quits
summary: Pollack fires him after his shoes are dirty from hand ball and Goodman quits in protest.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: But Glen was very graceful about it and bowed out. A funny thing happened though on that Pollack band. The manager, this guy's name was Bernie Foyer. And after we got through the Park Central Hotel we got on tour and we were playing in these theaters and dance halls and so forth. And Benny Goodman, Gil Rodin, Harry Goodman and myself used to room together, most all of the time. We used to play a lot of hand ball. And between shows one day at the Fox Brooklyn Theater we went upstairs on the roof and got a hand ball and were hitting it against the wall. And our uniform consisted of black and white shoes you know you had to put white on them to keep them clean and everything.
So we had to rush downstairs and go on stage we were in a hurry and I had to get out and sing a number and I think it was 'Sugar' or something. And by george my shoes were dirty. (LAUGHTER).

Ben Pollack fired me. See this Bernie Foyer wanted him to become a Rudy Valee you know and be a real bandleader style. Whereas he had been one of the guys before you know. Oh, he was a good drummer and everything. So Benny Goodman, I mean Benny Pollack fired me. He says, dirty shoes and

started hollering after the show. So he says, you've got two weeks' notice Jimmy, you know, I'm firing you. So Benny Goodman said, what did you say Ben Pollack? What? He says, I gave Jimmy his notice. He's got two weeks' notice. And Benny Goodman said, if you fire Jimmy you got my notice too. He says, I quit. Benny Goodman did.
So Benny Goodman quit, I got fired. (LAUGHTER).
